     4:
     5:/**

     9:export type { DayPhase };

    11:/**

    15:export function phaseFromTime(now: string, timezone: string): DayPhase {
    16:  return getDayPhase(now, timezone);
    17:}
    18:
    19:/** Default phase used before the API reports a time. */
    20:export const DEFAULT_PHASE: DayPhase = "day";
    21:
    22:/**
    23: * Backdrop art per phase.
    24: * aspect: art width / height. groundLine: where the open lawn starts, as a fraction of the art height from the top.
    25: * The backdrop lines the ground line up with the dog's feet, so update both when the art changes.
    26: */
    27:export const BACKDROP_BY_PHASE: Record<DayPhase, { src: string; aspect: number; groundLine: number }> = {
    28:  day: { src: "/assets/garden-day.webp", aspect: 923 / 2000, groundLine: 0.36 },
    29:  night: { src: "/assets/garden-night.webp", aspect: 923 / 2000, groundLine: 0.36 },
    30:};
    31:
    32:/** The default dog art. DogStage falls back to it when a mood image fails to load. */
    33:export const DOG_BASE_IMAGE = "/assets/dog-base.webp";
    34:
    35:/**
    36: * Dog art per mood. Every image shares the base art's canvas (1000x1300, transparent, same feet line),
    37: * so the ground line and accessory positions stay valid. Only sleepy has its own art today.
    38: */
    39:export const DOG_IMAGE_BY_MOOD: Record<DogMood, string> = {
    40:  joyful: DOG_BASE_IMAGE,
    41:  content: DOG_BASE_IMAGE,
    42:  sleepy: "/assets/dog-sleepy.webp",
    43:  attentive: DOG_BASE_IMAGE,
    44:};
    45:
    46:/**
    47: * TENTATIVE starting values, no design spec yet.
    48: * glow: opacity of the soft light behind the dog. playful: whether tap wiggle is allowed.
    49: * Motion itself lives in DogStage.css, keyed by mood class, transform/opacity only.
    50: */
    51:export const MOOD_LOOKS: Record<DogMood, { glow: number; playful: boolean }> = {
    52:  joyful: { glow: 0.85, playful: true },
    53:  content: { glow: 0.6, playful: true },
    54:  sleepy: { glow: 0.35, playful: true },
    55:  attentive: { glow: 0.25, playful: false },
    56:};
    57:
    58:/**
    59: * Two-column scene for phones and tablets held sideways (and any short landscape window).
    60: * Desktop (mouse) keeps the centred portrait column. index.css repeats this query for the layout rules; keep both in sync.
    61: */
    62:export const LANDSCAPE_MEDIA_QUERY =
    63:  "(orientation: landscape) and (hover: none) and (pointer: coarse), (orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 520px)";
    64:
    65:export type SceneLayout = "portrait" | "landscape";
    66:
    67:/**
    68: * Where the companion dog stands on each screen.
    69: * ground: the element whose top edge is the dog's feet line.
    70: * minHeight / maxHeight: TENTATIVE size limits. The max keeps the small source art from upscaling into blur and dominating tall phones.
    71: * ledge: the screen's content card leaves room above itself (--ledge-space) so the dog can stand on its top edge.
    72: *
    73: * Portrait: home = on the lawn just above the Today chips; ledge = on the top edge of the content card.
    74: * Landscape: the dog stays on the lawn in the left column on every screen. homeWide = on Home's chips;
    75: * lawn = on the .scene-ground marker, which sits at the same height as Home's chips so the dog doesn't jump between screens.
    76: */
    77:export const DOG_PLACEMENTS = {
    78:  home: { ground: ".home-layout__chips", minHeight: "clamp(120px, 26dvh, 320px)", maxHeight: "34dvh", ledge: false },
    79:  ledge: { ground: ".content-card", minHeight: "clamp(80px, 14dvh, 140px)", maxHeight: "34dvh", ledge: true },
    80:  homeWide: { ground: ".home-layout__chips", minHeight: "clamp(110px, 30dvh, 300px)", maxHeight: "46dvh", ledge: false },
    81:  lawn: { ground: ".scene-ground", minHeight: "clamp(110px, 30dvh, 300px)", maxHeight: "46dvh", ledge: false },
    82:} as const;
    83:
    84:export type DogPlacement = keyof typeof DOG_PLACEMENTS;
    85:
    86:/** Screens without the dog: the caretaker view, and the full-screen intro which has no scene at all. */
    87:const SCREENS_WITHOUT_DOG: readonly Screen[] = ["care", "cover", "dedication"];
    88:
    89:export function dogPlacementFor(screen: Screen, layout: SceneLayout = "portrait"): DogPlacement | null {
    90:  if (SCREENS_WITHOUT_DOG.includes(screen)) return null;
    91:  if (layout === "landscape") return screen === "home" ? "homeWide" : "lawn";
    92:  return screen === "home" ? "home" : "ledge";
    93:}
